title: SAR is different from negative number rounding for signed IDIV
summary: SAR preserves the sign bit. Shifting one bit right divides by two and rounds down. IDIV truncates the quotient toward zero.
applies: 64-bit mode for x86-64; Intel SDM Volume 1 and Volume 2
detail: Arithmetically shifting −3 to the right by one position gives −2, and the quotient of the signed integer −3 divided by 2 is −1.
boundary: If the disassembly biases negative values before SAR, the entire instruction sequence may be truncated toward zero.
relevance: When translating the disassembly into a high-level language, negative odd numbers are the smallest example that distinguishes the two types of rounding.
